queries: How do real estate fund IR teams automate ILPA DDQ responses when answers depend on live portfolio data like NAV, occupancy and debt maturities?
evidence: LLM web research (fund): DDQ tools rank for this topic: AutoRFP.ai (https://autorfp.ai/blog/best-ddq-automation-software-for-private-equity-firms), Tribble (https://tribble.ai/ddq-automation/ and https://tribble.ai/blog/automate-ddq-responses-fund-specific-evidence/), DiligenceVault, Dasseti, Ontra and Trapol8. All of them are built for generic PE or hedge-fund DDQs. Their answers come from approved fund documents, policies and prior DDQs. Tribble warns against firm-level boilerplate when the question needs date-sensitive or fund-specific evidence. Arphie (https://www.arphie.ai/blog/ddq-faq-investor-relations) only says in general terms that these tools connect to source systems for changing financial data. Nobody covers real estate funds. Nobody shows a DDQ answer pulling property-level numbers from the accounting or property system, with the source and an as-of date attached. Nobody covers the review gate when a DDQ answer conflicts with the last LP report.

queries: Who is liable and who must sign off when AI drafts the quarterly LP letter and variance commentary for a real estate fund?
evidence: LLM web research (fund): Vendor pages say AI can draft LP narrative and variance commentary: NextAutomation (https://nextautomation.us/blog/best-ai-tools-for-real-estate-fund-reporting), the AI Consulting Network (https://www.theaiconsultingnetwork.com/blog/automated-investment-reporting-ai-dashboards) and WorkWise (https://workwisesolutions.org/solutions/investor-reporting-engine.html). They claim 40–80 hours reduced to 2–4 hours, or an 80% cycle cut, with no evidence behind the figures. The AI Consulting Network's ChatGPT-prompts page (https://www.theaiconsultingnetwork.com/blog/chatgpt-prompts-real-estate-investor-reports) says there is no disclosure requirement and the GP stays responsible, and it goes no further. Missing: a review-gate design for who approves each claim, how every number ties to a source, how forward-looking statements and marketing-rule risk are handled, and how commentary stays consistent across LP classes. queries: How do we make sure an AI-drafted offering memorandum numbers tie back to the seller's rent roll and T-12 before it goes to buyers?
evidence: LLM web research (brokerage): The OM-generation results are tool listicles and form-fill generators: Ascendix (https://ascendix.com/blog/ai-real-estate-agents/), Kolena (https://www.kolena.com/blog/ai-in-commercial-real-estate/), DealDraft (https://www.dealdraft.online/ — $99/yr, 'enter your property details'), Plotdaily (https://plotdaily.com/ai-tools-for-commercial-real-estate) and Henry AI. They sell speed (4+ hours down to 5 minutes, or 50% faster). A.CRE (https://www.adventuresincre.com/ai-tools-commercial-real-estate/) names OM drafts as a first task that pays off. None of these cover a tie-out of every OM figure to the source rent roll, T-12 and lease. None cover broker review before release, handling of seller-confidential data in AI tools, or a record of which source backs each claim. Sageregroup (https://sageregroup.com/ai-tools-commercial-real-estate-investors/) only reminds readers to check the NDA.

queries: How can a commercial brokerage deploy AI agents on top of Salesforce or its existing CRM without changing its data model?
evidence: LLM web research (brokerage): TFSF Ventures (https://www.tfsfventures.com/blog/best-ai-agents-for-commercial-real-estate-brokerage-operations) says most platforms make brokerages adapt to the platform's data model. It describes Buildout's AI as task-specific, not agent-grade, because it does not monitor deals or act across sources. It does not show how to do this in practice. NextAutomation (https://nextautomation.us/blog/top-10-ai-tools-for-commercial-real-estate-agents) and A.CRE (https://www.adventuresincre.com/ai-tools-commercial-real-estate/) recommend a general LLM plus a CRM connector. Missing: what the agent may read versus write, a deal-status exception queue, who reviews comps and BOV drafts before they reach a client, and broker-team compliance. This overlaps with Prestyj's read/write boundary angle only as a brokerage deal-pipeline use case.

queries: Can AI handle CAM reconciliation for a commercial portfolio, including caps, exclusions and gross-ups, with a controller sign-off and audit trail?
evidence: LLM web research (owner-operator): Results are mostly vendor and small-tool pages: Datagrid (https://datagrid.com/blog/ai-lease-administrators-cam-reconciliation-billing), Creagentic (https://creagentic.ai/cam-reconciliation, $149/mo), CAM Recon (https://cam-recon.com/), Zedly (https://zedly.ai/blog/best-cam-reconciliation-software-for-commercial-landlords), Kognitos and RE BackOffice. Datagrid is the closest to a review-gate approach, with named reviewers and dispute records. SFAI Labs (https://sfailabs.com/guides/best-ai-accounting-automations-cre-ap-cam-reconciliations) calls CAM the one accounting task worth building for. Missing from institutional-owner content: how to read ambiguous lease CAM clauses, how to document the interpretation, and what the controller reviews versus what is auto-prepared. Also missing: tenant-dispute and audit-defense evidence packs, and a recovery-leakage baseline for multi-property portfolios. Claims like 'reduce errors by 95%' have no support.

queries: How should a real estate fund use AI to review third-party appraisals against internal valuations and flag divergent assumptions?
evidence: LLM web research (fund): The only substantive hit is a LeewayHertz table row (https://www.leewayhertz.com/ai-in-real-estate/) on extracting appraisal assumptions, comparing them with internal evidence and summarizing valuation variances. No dedicated article, vendor guide or practitioner walkthrough surfaced. It concerns CFO and valuation-committee work: NAV support, auditor and LP questions, and open-end fund valuation. Missing: which inputs to compare (cap rate, rent growth, lease-up), how to show divergence with sources, and how to log the reviewer's decision before the valuation is final.

queries: How do we check that AI-drafted capital call and distribution notices match the LPA and the fund administrator's numbers before they go out?
evidence: LLM web research (fund): Results are portal and software pages: Agora (https://agorareal.com/capital-calls/ and https://agorareal.com/compare/best-investor-reporting-software/), InvestorPortaLPro (https://investorportalpro.com/solutions/capital-call-software.html), and the AI-for-proptech page on Juniper Square (https://aiforproptech.com/capital-investor-relations/). They cover calculation, notice generation and portal delivery, and the proptech page says many portals add a chatbot and call it AI. NextAutomation (https://nextautomation.us/blog/best-ai-tools-for-real-estate-fund-reporting) positions an AI drafting layer above the portal. Missing: a control view for $500M+ funds on how the notice math is checked against LPA terms and admin records. Also missing: exceptions such as equalization, side letters and defaulting LPs, and who approves before release. Content is thin and written for syndicators and mid-market GPs.

queries: Can AI prepare lender compliance certificates across our property portfolio using each loan's own DSCR definitions and reporting requirements?
evidence: LLM web research (owner-operator): Search surfaced Docuity explicitly offering covenant certificates with calculation backups (https://docuity.ai/), while Moody's emphasizes lender-side monitoring (https://www.moodys.com/web/en/us/solutions/lending/commercial-real-estate.html). The broad certificate-generation angle is already covered. Inferred narrower gap: a borrower-side walkthrough spanning multiple lenders, contractual NOI adjustments, reporting calendars, amendments and officer certification, with a separate calculation workbook for each facility. This targets the owner's debt-reporting burden rather than quarter-end accounting.

queries: How can our real estate fund automatically identify which LP notices are triggered when we refinance, sell an asset or change a key person?
evidence: LLM web research (fund): Ontra already covers recurring and event-based side-letter obligations (https://www.ontra.ai/solutions/side-letters/); Zive describes extraction, routing and compliance-task triggers (https://www.zive.ai/products/docs-compliance/side-letter-obligation-tracking). Generic obligation tracking is therefore not a gap. Inferred opportunity: show how real estate transaction milestones become counsel-reviewed notice packages, including the contractual trigger, deadline, recipient list and evidence of delivery. The sampled pages did not demonstrate that asset-event-to-LP-notice sequence. Distinct from LP access permissions.

queries: Can AI turn our commercial leasing proposals into approval packages showing net effective rent, TI, commissions and variance from the asset business plan?
evidence: LLM web research (owner-operator): VTS describes proposal abstraction, cash-flow modeling and budget benchmarking (https://www.vts.com/for-ai), alongside AI extraction and portfolio intelligence (https://www.vts.com/ai). The opening is not another proposal-extraction article. Inferred content gap: a worked owner-side approval package comparing proposal versions, concession economics, upfront cash requirements and business-plan thresholds, including who must authorize an exception. The sampled pages describe capabilities rather than demonstrating this approval deliverable across the owner's existing financial models.

queries: How can our commercial brokerage automate weekly seller reports from CRM activity, broker emails, tours and buyer feedback?
evidence: LLM web research (brokerage): Buildout's owner's-report article explains automated branded marketing updates (https://www.buildout.com/blog-posts/buildouts-owners-reports-provide-transparency-and-clarity), and its broader automation page promotes connected deal and activity visibility (https://www.buildout.com/blog-posts/what-is-cre-brokerage-automation). Inferred gap: assembling a seller-facing narrative from activity distributed across systems, distinguishing marketing exposure from substantive buyer interest, and translating tour objections into broker-reviewed next steps. The sampled content does not walk through that cross-source reporting process. This is ongoing client service, not inbound qualification.

queries: Can AI reconcile our CRE brokerage's commission agreements, deal milestones and cash receipts to show what is earned, payable and overdue?
evidence: LLM web research (brokerage): CommercialEdge's commission guide details the administrative complexity of cash- and accrual-aligned distributions (https://www.commercialedge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/75/2022/11/CommercialEdge-Managing-the-Financial-Complexities-of-CRE-Brokerage-Commissions.pdf). Buildout promotes custom commission tiers, vouchers and earnings dashboards (https://go.buildout.com/brevitas/elevate-your-entire-brokerage). Inferred gap: an agreement-to-collection walkthrough covering lease commencement or installment conditions, co-broker obligations, overdue invoices and supporting evidence for finance. Existing sampled material explains commission systems more than this finished reconciliation work product. Scope is brokerage revenue operations, not fund waterfalls.

queries: How can a real estate fund automate allocator DDQs that require property-level operating data, not just answers from previous questionnaires?
evidence: LLM web research (fund): Ontra already markets private-markets DDQ automation and precedent libraries (https://www.ontra.ai/products/ddq-software/). DiligenceVault describes source-backed autofill, SME collaboration and compliance sign-off (https://fd-website-prod-001-h4hyhma6fxfsdwcc.a03.azurefd.net/solution/ai-powered-rfp-ddq-and-investor-reporting-automation/). Generic DDQ automation is crowded. Inferred narrower gap: answering real-estate-specific allocator requests that require current occupancy, lease rollover, leverage and operating metrics across assets, with explicit measurement dates and portfolio inclusion rules. The sampled pages did not demonstrate those property-data schedules being assembled alongside narrative answers.

queries: Can AI assemble our annual portfolio capital plan from property-manager requests, condition reports, bids and remaining hold periods?
evidence: LLM web research (owner-operator): Banner discusses AI-assisted capital-plan drafting and forecast-to-complete while retaining asset-manager allocation decisions (https://withbanner.com/home/blog/how-ai-is-changing-capex-management-for-cre-owners). JLL addresses portfolio-level retrofit prioritization and time-sequenced capital roadmaps (https://www.jll.de/content/dam/jll-com/documents/pdf/research/global/jll-streamline-sustainable-asset-enhancement-with-ai.pdf). Inferred gap: a worked annual capital-plan deliverable joining requested projects, bid assumptions, dependencies, hold periods and funded-versus-deferred scenarios. The opportunity is the reviewable planning package, not generic predictive maintenance or autonomous capital allocation.

queries: Can AI build a buyer shortlist for a commercial listing from our CRM notes and email history using each investor's current acquisition criteria?
evidence: LLM web research (brokerage): SourceDeck advertises verified buyer campaigns and staged outreach (https://sourcedeck.ai/); SuiteCRE promotes prospecting, CRM records and AI workflows (https://www.suitecre.com/). These establish adjacent competitive coverage, not an empty category. Inferred narrower gap: showing how private relationship notes and emails become dated institutional buyer mandates, how hard exclusions eliminate unsuitable buyers, and how each shortlisted buyer receives an evidence-backed fit explanation. The sampled product pages did not demonstrate that mandate-maintenance-to-shortlist sequence. This is outbound disposition targeting, not inbound lead qualification.
